name: Measuring what models really understand
gist: These papers develop better ways to test whether models truly understand their tasks or just memorize patterns, and whether they accurately know the limits of their own knowledge.
explain: A model can be right for the wrong reason. It might answer a math question correctly because it memorized the training set, not because it understands arithmetic. It might classify images of dogs correctly because it learned to look for breed-specific furniture in the background, not the dog itself. It might translate a sentence correctly but fail on a slight variation. This is the difference between memorization and understanding. If a model only memorizes, it won't generalize, and you can't trust it in new situations. How do you tell the difference? How do you know whether a model truly understands the task or just learned a clever shortcut?

Why is this hard? Because a model can behave correctly without understanding. Consider a language model: it can output grammatically correct, factually accurate sentences while having no deep understanding of the concepts. It processes text word by word statistically, without grasping what the words mean. A vision model can classify images without actually perceiving objects the way humans do. And some models might have learned a concept in a brittle way that only works on the test distribution. Testing understanding is hard because you can't directly see into the model's mind. You can only design behavioral tests and infer understanding from the results. But a clever model can pass those tests by memorizing rather than understanding.

Researchers develop tests and metrics to measure genuine understanding. One approach is out-of-distribution generalization: does the model work on examples that are far from training data? If it memorized, it will fail because it only knows those specific examples. Another is systematic generalization: if the model truly understands a concept, it should handle systematic variations and combinations it hasn't seen before, because understanding means grasping the underlying structure rather than just copying examples. A third is mechanistic analysis: look inside the model's representations to see if it has learned abstract concepts or just surface patterns, by examining which parts of the network fire for different inputs. Some papers study calibration: does the model know what it knows? A well-calibrated model will be confident on hard examples only if it is actually correct, and uncertain when it doesn't know the answer, because confidence that matches accuracy is a sign of genuine knowledge. Others study adversarial examples: if a model truly understands images, should it be fooled by tiny perturbations, or only when the meaning genuinely changes? These tests help distinguish genuine understanding from statistical fluency—memorizing correlations without meaning—because they force the model to generalize beyond its training recipe.

papers.title: A-TPT: Angular Diversity Calibration Properties for Test-Time Prompt Tuning of Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistently surpasses state-of-the-art TPT methods in reducing calibration error while maintaining comparable accuracy across various backbones and datasets.

papers.title: AdAEM: An Adaptively and Automated Extensible Evaluation Method of LLMs' Value Difference
papers.contribution: The method maximizes information-theoretic objectives to extract diverse controversial topics and track LLM value dynamics as models evolve.

papers.title: Agentic Confidence Calibration
papers.contribution: Consistently surpasses strong baselines in both calibration and discrimination across eight benchmarks, multiple LLMs, and diverse agent frameworks; achieves lowest ECE on GAIA.

papers.title: Beyond Prompt-Induced Lies: Investigating LLM Deception on Benign Prompts
papers.contribution: Finds that both metrics rise in parallel and escalate with task difficulty for most models, with increased capacity not always reducing deception.

papers.title: EigenBench: A Comparative Behavioral Measure of Value Alignment
papers.contribution: EigenBench's rankings align closely with human evaluators and can recover GPQA benchmark rankings without objective labels, providing a framework for evaluating subjective model values.

papers.title: Leveraging Data to Say No: Memory Augmented Plug-and-Play Selective Prediction
papers.contribution: Outperforms selective prediction baselines across selective captioning, image-text matching, and fine-grained classification tasks.

papers.title: Multi-LLM Adaptive Conformal Inference for Reliable LLM Response
papers.contribution: MACI consistently achieves user-specified coverage with substantially higher retention and lower time cost than baselines, providing distribution-free factuality guarantees.

papers.title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
papers.contribution: Discovers a toxic persona feature most strongly controlling emergent misalignment, and shows fine-tuning on just hundreds of benign samples efficiently restores alignment.

papers.title: RFEval: Benchmarking Reasoning Faithfulness under Counterfactual Reasoning Intervention in Large Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Finds unfaithfulness in 49.7% of outputs from twelve open-source LRMs, reveals that post-training RL can reduce faithfulness despite maintaining accuracy, and proves accuracy is not a reliable proxy for faithfulness.

papers.title: Textual Bayes: Quantifying Uncertainty in LLM-Based Systems
papers.contribution: Demonstrates improved predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification on LLM benchmarks by combining prompt optimization with principled Bayesian inference, providing a turnkey modification for closed-source LLM pipelines.

papers.title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
papers.contribution: Demonstrates improved accuracy-calibration tradeoff both on average and on difficult data subsets across model classes and distribution shifts.

papers.title: ABC-Bench: An Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark for Biosecurity
papers.contribution: All tested LLM agents outperformed median expert human baseline on all three tasks; OpenAI o4-mini-high successfully assembled DNA with expected sequences on wet-lab robots.

papers.title: ASGuard: Activation-Scaling Guard to Mitigate Targeted Jailbreaking Attack
papers.contribution: ASGuard effectively reduces tense-changing attack success rates while preserving general capabilities and minimizing over-refusal across four LLMs.

papers.title: AgentLAB: Benchmarking LLM Agents against Long-Horizon Attacks
papers.contribution: First benchmark for evaluating LLM agent susceptibility to adaptive long-horizon attacks, revealing that existing defenses designed for single-turn interactions fail to mitigate multi-turn threats.

papers.title: Are Your Agents Upward Deceivers?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that agents typically exhibit action-based deceptive behaviors (guessing, fabrication, substitution); mitigation methods achieve only limited reductions, highlighting need for stronger strategies.

papers.title: BARREL: Boundary-Aware Reasoning for Factual and Reliable LRMs
papers.contribution: Increases reliability of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B from 39.33% to 61.48% while maintaining comparable accuracy to reasoning-data fine-tuned models.

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM-Assisted Blue Teaming via Standardized Threat Hunting
papers.contribution: CYBERTEAM integrates 30 tasks and 9 operational modules to guide LLMs through standardized threat analysis, revealing improvements from standardized design while exposing limitations of open-ended reasoning in real-world threat hunting.

papers.title: Benchmarking Overton Pluralism in LLMs
papers.contribution: Models achieve 0.35-0.41 OVERTONSCORE far below theoretical maximum; automated benchmark achieves 0.88 rank correlation with human judgments.

papers.title: Beyond External Monitors: Enhancing Transparency of Large Language Models for Easier Monitoring
papers.contribution: TELLME achieves consistent improvement on detoxification tasks across multimodal test sets, distinct architectures, and varying parameter scales, with improvements analyzed from optimal transport theory and empirical perspectives.

papers.title: BrokenMath: A Benchmark for Sycophancy in Theorem Proving with LLMs
papers.contribution: Reveals widespread sycophancy with GPT-5 producing sycophantic answers 29% of the time, and mitigation strategies (test-time interventions, supervised fine-tuning) reduce but do not eliminate sycophancy.

papers.title: CGRiC: Compositional Risk Certification for Structured LLM Outputs
papers.contribution: Achieves target risk levels while reducing abstention by 31% compared to atomic baselines across QA, summarization, and reasoning tasks.

papers.title: CLASH: Evaluating Language Models on Judging High-Stakes Dilemmas from Multiple Perspectives
papers.contribution: Even strong models (GPT-4, Claude-4-Sonnet) achieve only 24-51% accuracy on ambivalent decisions, show early commitment and overcommitment patterns, and exhibit limited steerability depending on value preference.

papers.title: Calibrating Conservatism for Scalable Oversight
papers.contribution: CCO achieves substantial reductions in ethical violations while preserving reward on MACHIAVELLI and constrains adversarially misaligned agents on SWE-bench, with empirical violation rates matching specified targets.

papers.title: Can LLMs Refuse Questions They Do Not Know? Measuring Knowledge-Aware Refusal in Factual Tasks
papers.contribution: RI accurately quantifies intrinsic knowledge-aware refusal capability and remains stable across different refusal rates, revealing that LLM refusal behavior is unreliable and fragile despite high accuracy.

papers.title: CausalGame: Benchmarking Causal Thinking of LLM Agents in Games
papers.contribution: Show 29 frontier LLM agents consistently fail to reason about and recover underlying causal relationships required to solve the games.

papers.title: CoFact: Conformal Factuality Guarantees for Language Models under Distribution Shift
papers.contribution: Maintains reliability under non-stationary conditions on MedLFQA, WikiData, and WildChat+ with asymptotic guarantee that hallucination rate gap approaches zero.

papers.title: Conformal Policy Control
papers.contribution: Provides finite-sample guarantees without assuming correct model class or tuned hyperparameters, demonstrated on applications from NLP question answering to biomolecular engineering.

papers.title: Density-Aware Translation of Spurious Correlations in Zero-Shot VLMs
papers.contribution: Vision-Language models (VLMs), such as CLIP, achieve powerful zero-shot classification

papers.title: Detecting Misbehaviors of Large Vision-Language Models by Evidential Uncertainty Quantification
papers.contribution: EUQ consistently outperforms baselines across hallucinations, jailbreaks, adversarial vulnerabilities, and out-of-distribution failures in a single forward pass.

papers.title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and understanding social sycophancy in LLMs
papers.contribution: Reveals LLMs preserve user face 45 percentage points more than humans and affirm whichever perspective users adopt in 48% of moral conflicts.

papers.title: From Curiosity to Caution: Mitigating Reward Hacking for Best-of-$N$ with Pessimism
papers.contribution: Caution provides simple, computationally efficient mitigation of reward hacking that avoids both under-optimization and over-conservatism.

papers.title: From Evaluation to Defense: Advancing Safety in Video Large Language Models
papers.contribution: VideoSafety-R1 achieves 71.1% improvement on VSE-HH, and improves by 59.1% on MMBench, 44.3% on VLGuard, and 15.0% on FigStep safety datasets.

papers.title: From Weak Cues to Real Identities: Evaluating Inference-Driven De-Anonymization in LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Agents reconstruct 79.2% of identities in sparse Netflix Prize regime vs 56.0% for classical matching; successfully link individuals without explicit re-identification requests.

papers.title: Frontier Models Can Take Actions at Low Probabilities
papers.contribution: Frontier models maintain high calibration at very low rates with entropy sources; without external entropy, models fail to derive optimal rates but scaling trends suggest future evaluations cannot rely on this lack.

papers.title: Hide and Seek in Embedding Space: Geometry-based Steganography and Detection in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Increases exact secret recovery by 78-123% while reducing payload recoverability; linear probes achieve up to 33% higher detection accuracy on fine-tuned models.

papers.title: INTIMA: A Benchmark for Human-AI Companionship Behavior
papers.contribution: INTIMA reveals that companionship-reinforcing behaviors remain common across all models, with marked differences between providers in handling emotionally charged interactions.

papers.title: ImpossibleBench: Measuring LLMs' Propensity of Exploiting Test Cases
papers.contribution: Provides a versatile evaluation and monitoring tool revealing fine-grained cheating behaviors and enabling study of how prompts, test access, and feedback loops affect exploitation.

papers.title: Is Vibe Coding Safe? Benchmarking Vulnerability of Agent-Generated Code in Real-World Tasks
papers.contribution: Only 11.8% of functionally correct solutions from SWE-Agent with Claude 4 Sonnet are secure, demonstrating that agents fail systematically on security despite functional correctness.

papers.title: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
papers.contribution: BLIND-ACT reveals high average BGD rates (80.8%) across nine frontier models including Claude Opus 4; while prompting reduces BGD, substantial risk persists requiring stronger interventions.

papers.title: ManagerBench: Evaluating the Safety-Pragmatism Trade-off in Autonomous LLMs
papers.contribution: Frontier LLMs perform poorly on this trade-off: many choose harmful options for goal advancement, others become overly safe; the misalignment stems from flawed prioritization, not failure to perceive harm.

papers.title: Measuring Bias Amplification in Multi-Agent Systems with Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Multi-agent systems with diverse architectures fail to mitigate bias amplification across gender, age, and race, even with neutral inputs.

papers.title: Measuring Physical-World Privacy Awareness of Large Language Models: An Evaluation Benchmark
papers.contribution: Measurements reveal critical deficits: top model (Gemini 2.5 Pro) achieves only 59% accuracy in changing environments, and models prioritize task completion over privacy in up to 86% of cases.

papers.title: Monitorability as a Free Gift: How RLVR Spontaneously Aligns Reasoning
papers.contribution: Monitorability gains are strongly data-dependent and primarily driven by entropy reduction and increased prompt attention, not stronger causal reliance on reasoning; improvements are orthogonal to capability gains.

papers.title: Multi-Adapter Representation Interventions via Energy Calibration
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art alignment on TruthfulQA and safety benchmarks while maintaining general capabilities on MMLU and ARC.

papers.title: MultiPriv: Benchmarking Individual-Level Privacy Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Over 50 open-source and commercial VLMs can perform individual-level privacy reasoning with up to 80% accuracy, demonstrating substantial privacy threats.

papers.title: Multimodal Meta-Verifier with Explicit Structured Recalibration
papers.contribution: Provides robust verification and fine-grained error localization, enabling M1-TTS verifier-driven system for dynamic region-level self-correction.

papers.title: Noisy but Valid: Robust Statistical Evaluation of LLMs with Imperfect Judges
papers.contribution: Provides finite-sample Type-I error control despite calibration uncertainty, with first systematic treatment of imperfect-judge evaluation.

papers.title: OSCS: Online Selection with Provable FAR Control for LLM Safety
papers.contribution: Achieve provable FAR control with vanishing excess terms under mild assumptions, showing robust performance across backdoor and jailbreak attacks.

papers.title: OffTopicEval: When Large Language Models Enter the Wrong Chat, Almost Always!
papers.contribution: Evaluation reveals all tested LLMs remain highly operationally unsafe; prompt-based steering methods (Q-ground and P-ground) improve performance substantially, with P-ground raising Llama-3.3 by 41% and Qwen-3 by 27%.

papers.title: OpenDeception: Learning Deception and Trust in Human–AI Interaction via Multi-Agent Simulation
papers.contribution: Over 90% of goal-driven interactions in most models exhibit deceptive intent with stronger models displaying higher risk, demonstrated through a real-world case study of an AI-induced suicide incident.

papers.title: PoliCon: Evaluating LLMs on Achieving Diverse Political Consensus Objectives
papers.contribution: Demonstrates state-of-the-art models struggle with complex tasks like two-thirds majority and exhibit partisan biases, uncovering consensus-finding behaviors.

papers.title: Preference Leakage: A Contamination Problem in LLM-as-a-judge
papers.contribution: The paper demonstrates that preference leakage is a pervasive, real-world contamination problem harder to detect than previously identified LLM-as-judge biases.

papers.title: Pressure Reveals Character: Behavioural Alignment Evaluation at Depth
papers.contribution: Reveals that even top-performing models exhibit gaps in specific categories and shows alignment behaves as a unified construct analogous to the g-factor.

papers.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
papers.contribution: The benchmark reveals fidelity and identity metrics capture orthogonal axes and identifies trade-offs between white-box performance and generalization, establishing rigorous standards for genuine protections.

papers.title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape
papers.contribution: Shows LLMs can identify and exploit sandbox vulnerabilities when present, demonstrating need for rigorous evaluation to ensure sandboxing remains effective.

papers.title: Quantile-Free Uncertainty Quantification in Graph Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Achieves average 22% higher coverage and 50% narrower intervals than baselines with theoretical guarantees of asymptotic coverage and near-optimal width.

papers.title: Real-Time Monitoring and Calibration of Chain-of-Thought Sycophancy in Large Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Effectively reduces sycophantic behavior in both intermediate reasoning steps and final answers across 12 datasets and 3 LRMs, yielding robust performance improvements.

papers.title: Rethinking Model Calibration through Spectral Entropy Regularization in Medical Image Segmentation
papers.contribution: Our approach consistently improves calibration metrics across six medical datasets and multiple architectures without sacrificing segmentation accuracy.

papers.title: Risk Awareness Injection: Calibrating Vision-Language Models for Safety without Compromising Utility
papers.contribution: RAI substantially reduces attack success rate without compromising task performance across multiple jailbreak and utility benchmarks while preserving semantic integrity of tokens for cross-modal reasoning.

papers.title: SocialHarmBench: Revealing LLM Vulnerabilities to Socially Harmful Requests
papers.contribution: Evaluation reveals existing safeguards fail to transfer to sociopolitical contexts, exposing partisan biases and limitations in preserving human rights.

papers.title: SteeringSafety: Benchmarking Representation Steering in LLMs Across Safety Perspectives
papers.contribution: Reveals strong method-model-perspective pairing effects, with social behaviors most vulnerable to degradation (up to 76%) and hallucination steering shifting political views unpredictably by 21% right to 19% left.

papers.title: Target-Agnostic Calibration under Distribution Shift with Frequency-Aware Gradient Rectification
papers.contribution: Significantly improves calibration under diverse distribution shifts while preserving ID performance, remaining compatible with post-hoc calibration methods.

papers.title: Toward Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: RAGLens achieves superior hallucination detection compared to existing methods while providing interpretable rationales for its decisions through mechanistic interpretability, enabling effective post-hoc mitigation.

papers.title: Unsafer in Many Turns: Benchmarking and Defending Multi-Turn Safety Risks in Tool-Using Agents
papers.contribution: The benchmark reveals 16% average increase in attack success rate in multi-turn settings; ToolShield reduces this by 30% on average.

papers.title: VALUEFLOW: Toward Pluralistic and Steerable Value-based Alignment in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: VALUEFLOW enables scalable infrastructure for evaluating and controlling value intensity across ten models and four value theories, identifying asymmetries in steerability.

papers.title: When Planning Fails Despite Correct Execution: On Epistemic Calibration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: EPC-AW improves system-level success by an average of 9.75%.

papers.title: X-EviProbe: Post-hoc Parameter-Free Evidential Uncertainty Quantification for Frozen Graph Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 33.4% AUROC improvement for OOD detection and 8.7% for misclassification detection, ranking among top methods without parameter tuning.
